relevance_note: This is a single-centre retrospective review of anakinra treatment in 47 patients whose diagnoses are SJIA, CAPS, MKD, SURF, PIMS-TS and other conditions ("Other AID, Blau syndrome and Pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum and acne syndrome"); TNFAIP3, A20 and HA20 are never mentioned, so no in-scope person is described.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; no script transcribed any table. A case-insensitive search for 'TNFAIP3', 'A20', 'haploinsufficiency' and 'HA20' found no match (the only hit was the DOI string 'NEJMoa2021680' in reference 36). The paper has no supplementary material section. Only the publications row is filled; the other tables are empty. cohort_size_as_stated = 47 is the analysed cohort ('From 47 patients (27 female patients) who fulfilled inclusion criteria'); the authors also state 60 patients were prescribed anakinra, of whom 13 were excluded. n_patients_reported left null because the paper states no number of TNFAIP3-variant patients. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the CAPS section cites reference (30) (Fingerhutova et al. 2019, a Muckle-Wells family report) after 'Two patients required dose escalation (to 200 mg/day) in order to maintain disease inactivity (30).', but the paper does not explicitly say these patients were described earlier. No contradictions found.

study_type.span: Clinical data from electronic records were retrospectively reviewed for patients treated with anakinra over the past 6 years for autoinflammatory diseases (AID).

cohort_size_as_stated.span: From 47 eligible patients (27 female patients), 32 were children.
